title: Selected finite relative affine presentation
statement:
Let $S$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme and let $f\colon X\to S$ be a morphism of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. The following finitely many objects exist, and $\mathsf R_X$ denotes one CHOICE of them, fixed once and for all (a citer may prescribe some of the choices, e.g. the base cover, provided they have the stated properties; $\mathsf R_X$ depends on the choices).
(i) A finite affine open cover $S=V_1\cup\dots\cup V_m$, $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$; it exists because $S$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover].
(ii) For each $a$, a finite affine open cover $f^{-1}(V_a)=U_{a1}\cup\dots\cup U_{an_a}$, $U_{ab}=\operatorname{Spec}A_{ab}$; it exists because $f$ is quasi-compact, so $f^{-1}(V_a)$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-morphism-preimage-qc-open], [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover].
(iii) For each chart, a finite presentation $A_{ab}\cong R_a[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_r)$ as $R_a$-algebras; it exists because $f$ is locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], so $R_a\to A_{ab}$ is of finite presentation [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation].
(iv) For each pair of charts $U,U'$, finitely many elements $h_k\in\mathcal O_X(U)$, $h'_k\in\mathcal O_X(U')$ with $D_U(h_k)=D_{U'}(h'_k)$ and $U\cap U'=\bigcup_kD_U(h_k)$; they exist because $X$ is quasi-separated ($f$ quasi-separated and $S$ quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2)), so $U\cap U'$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-separated-affine-cover-criterion] (1) and is covered by opens basic in both charts [lem-sc-affine-inter-principal-both].
(v) For each such basic overlap, the two mutually inverse ring isomorphisms $\mathcal O_X(U)_{h_k}\rightleftarrows\mathcal O_X(U')_{h'_k}$ given by restriction on $D_U(h_k)=D_{U'}(h'_k)$.
$\mathsf R_X$ is the record of the data (i)-(v) together with the finitely many identity, inverse and cocycle equations they satisfy (identity on the diagonal overlaps, (v) mutually inverse, and compatibility of the isomorphisms on triple overlaps).
